messages:
devin: hey folks — quick payroll/tax question. I converted from contractor (based in India, paid through vendor platform) to FT-US on 2025-09-01. Contractor invoices were paid in INR via vendor payouts. I just checked my paystub and year-to-date withholding looks low; payroll applied a retro salary adjustment but theres still a gap. Will the contractor earnings show up on my W-2? worried about 1099 vs W-2 and potential double-tax. any guidance?

jen (People Ops): thanks for flagging, @devin. short answer: contractor payments made to a vendor entity generally do not appear on your W-2. but let me loop payroll + tax counsel to confirm on the retro adjustments. can you paste the vendor invoice id or the PAY ticket?

devin: invoice IDs: INV-9876, INV-1002. payroll ticket created earlier is PAY-3129. here's the paystub snippet (redacted):

```
Gross pay (YTD): $42,500
Federal withholding (YTD): $1,200
Retro adjustment (Sep): +$8,000
Net pay (Sep): $5,600
```

alex (Payroll): @devin thanks — we see PAY-3129. Quick notes: 1) If payments were processed to a vendor (company) and not to you as an independent contractor on a US 1099-NEC, they typically aren't reported on your W-2. 2) If you were personally paid (1099-NEC) earlier, that would be separate from W-2 wages. 3) Retro adjustments to convert contractor earnings into employee salary can be handled as taxable wages on W-2 if payroll team made them as employee compensation. We need to confirm how the vendor payments were categorized.

maria (Tax Counsel): adding a tax perspective: if you were paid to an Indian contractor entity, that income was generally sourced/withheld per local rules and wouldn't be on US W-2. However, for US tax residency purposes (if you became a US tax resident after switching), you may have reporting obligations. Important: any retroactive compensation processed on payroll as "employee wages" for 2025 will appear on the 2025 W-2. Previous vendor payments are not converted retroactively unless we issued a correction. If you received a 1099-NEC for personal services in the US, that remains separate.

devin: OK. so action items? Im worried about an under-withheld balance when I file. Also saw a line in the paystub notes: "withholding correction pending". what should I expect?

alex (Payroll): action plan: 1) payroll will audit PAY-3129 and confirm whether INV-9876/INV-1002 were paid to your vendor company or to you personally. 2) if retro wages were posted as employee compensation, we'll confirm if additional federal/state withholding was applied; if not, we can run a supplemental withholding to cover the gap (or set up a catch-up in upcoming pay cycles). 3) we'll coordinate with Tax Counsel for any filing/1099 implications. ETA: 2 business days. tagging @payroll-bot for the audit job.

payroll-bot: PAY-3129 audit queued — assigned to alex. expected completion: 48 hours. :gear:

jen (People Ops): will follow up once payroll confirms. @devin if you expect a large balance, consider setting aside funds for estimated tax or we can arrange voluntary withholding. also let us know if you received any 1099s or vendor statements — that helps the audit. :thumbsup:

devin: thanks everyone — I have the vendor payment receipts and one 1099-NEC issued in July that looks like it was issued to me personally (odd). I'll attach to PAY-3129. appreciate the quick triage. :relieved:
